source_en: Opening the salon.
Collecting hair product from the depot.
Home styling appointment.
Trading haircuts at the market.
Hunting for beauty supplies.
Back from a supply run.
Keeping the salon open.
Bringing filler to the salon.
Finishing a procedure at home.
Tram ticket clerk. Going home.
My first ever haircut.
Collecting maternity leave papers.
Selling the salon chairs.
Visiting my grandchildren.
Job interview at the bread factory.
Throwing out all my mirrors.
Collecting my hairdresser's pension.
Getting my old face back.
Officer! Your eyebrows are fascinating today. Have you considered threading?
Papers. Also: moisturise. This air is destroying everyone's pores.
New procedure last night. Ignore the swelling. It is part of the process.
You look tired, officer. Take my card. First session is free.
Do not stare. Beauty requires sacrifice, and I am very committed.
Something is wrong with the mirrors in this city. They lie now.
You are STARING at me. Do not. Stare. At. Me.
I look incredible. Say it before you stamp anything.
Each one is an improvement. Stop making that face.
You do not get to judge me. Stamp it and look away.
Everything else has rotted. I am STILL PERFECT.
I know what I look like. I KNOW. Stamp it.
Wonderful! Visit the salon. I could do a lot with you.
Smart choice. Judgement is a two-way street.
Good instincts, officer. Or good taste, at least.
This is aesthetic discrimination. I am filing a complaint.
I have tweezers in my pocket. You cannot stop the process.
So close… to the jawline I wanted…
Just needed… one more… adjustment…
Where are you coming from?
The salon on Rustaveli. Two perms, a colour, and my own jaw.
The river market. I traded a haircut for filler. Tell no one.
The salon. I was working on myself. I lost track of hours.
My salon on Plekhanov Avenue. The light is good for colour.
The barracks. I cut soldiers' hair now. The salon closed weeks ago.
Home. I shut the salon last month. No one left worth cutting.
The supply depot. Do not ask what I bought.
From the mirror. I have been working on myself. Non-stop.
I do not remember leaving. I was in the mirror a long time.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Jaw bruising. Self-administered filler. It settles by Sunday.
Some swelling, numb cheeks. My pain threshold is up. A good sign.
I cannot feel my cheekbones. Irrelevant. The proportions are finally correct.
Nothing. I have never had a procedure. All natural.
No swelling. A polyclinic surgeon did my last injection.
I feel wonderful. I stopped all procedures a month ago.
No symptoms. These are improvements. There is a difference.
They are not symptoms. They are upgrades.
My body is cooperating fully with the vision.
Your skin is dehydrated, officer. Drink water. Use SPF. I beg you.
I opened the salon at six. I will close it when the city does.
The good products are gone. I improvise. Results are mostly fine.
People say I look different. I look optimised.
My salon mirror cracked this morning. I took it as a challenge.
I am not finished. This is a work in progress.
Stop looking at my face. I can see you looking.
You have an opinion about my face. Keep it.
I am the last beautiful thing in this district.
